problem: The list says header, nav, main, aside and footer are landmarks without the caveat that a header or footer nested inside an article, section or aside is not a landmark. The same section already tells students a header may repeat inside an article, so a student can build a nested header and wrongly call it a banner landmark. The list also omits the search/form landmarks without saying the list is only the common ones.
fix: Say: the page-level header, nav, main, aside and footer are landmarks (banner, navigation, main, complementary, contentinfo); a header or footer inside an article or section is not a landmark. Add that a form or search region with an accessible name is also a landmark.

problem: The bullet reads 'preload: hint, none, metadata or auto', which mixes the meaning ('a hint') with the attribute values. A student may write preload='hint'.
fix: Say: preload takes the values none, metadata or auto (empty string behaves like auto); it is a hint to the browser about how much of the file to fetch early.

problem: 'kind= captions gives sound descriptions and speech for deaf viewers' invites confusion with the separate kind='descriptions', which is audio description of visual content. Captions carry dialogue plus important non-speech sounds, not 'sound descriptions'.
fix: Say: kind='captions' gives the dialogue plus important non-speech sounds (a door slams, music starts) for deaf and hard-of-hearing viewers or when sound is off. kind='descriptions' is the different track that speaks descriptions of the visuals for blind users.

problem: The answer allows only sections for the comment blocks. The HTML standard itself lists a user-submitted comment as one of the classic examples of an article, so a student who answers 'each comment is an article' is following standard textbooks and would be marked wrong here.
fix: Keep the reasoning but accept both: the story is definitely an article; each comment that stands on its own (has its own heading, could be read or linked alone) may be an article, and a section is the right choice when the block merely groups part of the story. Say which choice you are defending and why.

problem: figure, details, time, mark, progress and meter are listed under a heading about named regions, but none of them is a landmark region. A student may come away thinking figure or progress is read as a page region.
fix: Split the list: keep header, nav, main, section, article, aside, footer under named regions, and give figure/figcaption, details/summary, time, mark, progress, meter their own short list headed 'Other named elements (not regions)'.
